﴿Dhalikum tu'azuna bihi﴾: that is, you are commanded with it, so do it as an obligation.

﴿Fa-man lam yajid fa-siyamu shahrayni mutatabi'ayni﴾: that is, whoever does not find a slave, either because none exists or because its price is high, the obligation is fasting two consecutive months.

﴿Min qabli an yatamassa﴾: that is, before intercourse with her.

﴿Fa-man lam yasta'* ﴾: that is, fasting, due to illness or old age.

﴿Fa-it'amu sittina miskinan﴾: that is, before intercourse he must feed sixty poor people, giving each poor person a mudd of wheat or two mudds of other than wheat, such as dates, barley, and similar staple foods of the people of the land.

﴿Dhalik﴾: that is, what has preceded of the explanation of the ruling on zihar, which was legislated for you.

﴿Li-tu'minu bi-Allahi wa rasulihi﴾: that is, because obedience is faith, and disobedience is disbelief.

﴿Wa tilka hudud Allah﴾: that is, the rulings of His law.

﴿Wa lil-kafirina 'adhabun alim﴾: that is, for those who disbelieve in them and deny them there is a painful punishment, that is, one that causes pain.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Qad sami'a Allah﴾: These noble verses were revealed concerning Khawlah bint Tha'labah al-Ansariyyah and her husband Aws ibn al-Samit, brother of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with them all. Her husband Aws had declared her unlawful, and he said to her in anger, not in a fixed manner, "You are to me like the back of my mother." Zihar at that time was a divorce. The woman had young children, and she and her husband had advanced in age. She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining to him of what her husband had said, and she mentioned to the Messenger ﷺ her weakness, her husband's weakness, and the weakness of her young children. She kept returning to the Messenger ﷺ and arguing with him about her case and her husband's case, until these four verses at the opening of Surah al-Mujadilah were revealed, by which the surah is named, so it is called Surah al-Mujadilah with a kasra on the dal, and it is also permissible to pronounce it with a fatha. Second: this saying is a lie, a falsehood, and a hateful utterance, and the one who says it is sinful, so let him repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness.

Third: were it not for Allah's pardon and forgiveness toward His servants and the believers, and His forgiveness of those who repent, He would punish them for this false and baseless utterance.

Fourth: upon those who declare their wives unlawful and then return to what they said, that is, who resolve to have intercourse with her after the zihar, the obligation upon them before intercourse is to free a slave, whether male or female, young or old, but it must be a believer, not a disbeliever. Whoever does not find a slave, either because none exists or because its price is high, then fasting two consecutive months suffices for him. If he is unable due to a condition affecting him, then the obligation is to feed sixty poor people, giving each poor person a mudd of wheat or half a sa' of other than wheat, such as barley, dates, and similar; all of this must be before they touch one another, by way of applying the absolute (mutlaq) to the restricted (muqayyad), since the first is restricted by "before touching," so this latter is understood in its light.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Allah's answering His allies by relieving their distress and fulfilling their needs; to Him belongs praise and thanks.

2. The prohibition of zihar as an abhorrent, false, and baseless utterance, so repentance from it is obligatory.

3. Explanation of the ruling for one who has made zihar: he must free a slave before he has intercourse with the wife he declared unlawful. If he does not find a believing slave, he fasts two consecutive months from crescent to crescent; if the consecutiveness is broken by illness, he resumes and builds upon what he has fasted. If he is unable due to illness or the like, he feeds sixty poor people, giving each poor person separately a mudd of wheat or two mudds of other than wheat, such as barley or dates.

4. If the one who made zihar has intercourse before paying the expiation, he has sinned, so let him seek forgiveness from his Lord and pay his expiation. There is nothing further upon him, based on the authentic hadith in al-Tirmidhi.

5. Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is faith, and disobedience to Allah and His Messenger is disbelief.

She kept returning to the Messenger ﷺ and arguing with him about her case and her husband's case, until these four verses at the opening of Surah al-Mujadilah were revealed, by which the surah is named, so it is called Surah al-Mujadilah with a kasra on the dal, and it is also permissible to pronounce it with a fatha. Allah, Exalted is He, addressed His Messenger: ﴿Qad sami'a Allah qawla allati tujadiluka fi zawjiha﴾: that is, Allah has indeed heard the words of the woman who argues with you, that is, who comes back to you, concerning her husband who declared her unlawful. ﴿Wa tashtaki ila Allah﴾, after you had said to her, "By Allah, I have not been commanded anything regarding your case," she complained to Allah of the weakness of her condition.

﴿Wa Allah yasma'u tahawurakuma﴾: that is, your returning to one another in conversation, and He answered you. ﴿Inna Allaha Sami'un Basir﴾: that is, He hears the words of His servants and knows their circumstances. This is the ruling on zihar, so understand it and act upon it.

First: that zihar, which is a man's saying to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother," does not make her his mother, since his mother is the one who bore him and came forth from her womb, and a wife is never a mother in any circumstance.

Second: this saying is a lie, a falsehood, and a hateful utterance, and the one who says it is sinful, so let him repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness.

Third: were it not for Allah's pardon and forgiveness toward His servants and the believers, and His forgiveness of those who repent, He would punish them for this false and baseless utterance.

Fourth: upon those who declare their wives unlawful and then return to what they said, that is, who resolve to have intercourse with her after the zihar, the obligation upon them before intercourse is to free a slave, whether male or female, young or old, but it must be a believer, not a disbeliever. Whoever does not find a slave, either because none exists or because its price is high, then fasting two consecutive months suffices for him. If he is unable due to a condition affecting him, then the obligation is to feed sixty poor people, giving each poor person a mudd of wheat or half a sa' of other than wheat, such as barley, dates, and similar; all of this must be before they touch one another, by way of applying the absolute (mutlaq) to the restricted (muqayyad), since the first is restricted by "before touching," so this latter is understood in its light.

His saying, ﴿Dhalika li-tu'minu bi-Allahi wa rasulihi﴾: that is, what has preceded of the explanation of the ruling on zihar was legislated by Him for you so that you believe in Allah and His Messenger, since faith is belief, speech, and action; obedience to Allah and His Messenger is faith, and disobedience to them is disbelief. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Wa tilka hudud Allah﴾: that is, do not transgress them, but stop at them. ﴿Wa lil-kafirina bi-ha al-mu'tadina lahā 'adhabun alim﴾: that is, for those who disbelieve in them and transgress them there is a painful punishment, that is, one with painful, aching torment, as recompense for their transgression of Allah's limits.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Allah's answering His allies by relieving their distress and fulfilling their needs; to Him belongs praise and thanks.

2. The prohibition of zihar as an abhorrent, false, and baseless utterance, so repentance from it is obligatory.

3. Explanation of the ruling for one who has made zihar: he must free a slave before he has intercourse with the wife he declared unlawful. If he does not find a believing slave, he fasts two consecutive months from crescent to crescent; if the consecutiveness is broken by illness, he resumes and builds upon what he has fasted. If he is unable due to illness or the like, he feeds sixty poor people, giving each poor person separately a mudd of wheat or two mudds of other than wheat, such as barley or dates.

4. If the one who made zihar has intercourse before paying the expiation, he has sinned, so let him seek forgiveness from his Lord and pay his expiation. There is nothing further upon him, based on the authentic hadith in al-Tirmidhi.

5. Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is faith, and disobedience to Allah and His Messenger is disbelief.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 58, verses 5–7:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Inna alladhina yuhadduna Allah wa rasulahu﴾ (Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger): that is, they contradict Allah and His Messenger and act as enemies to them both.

﴿Kubitu kama kubita alladhina min qablihim﴾ (they will be humiliated as those before them were humiliated): that is, they will be abased and disgraced as those before them were abased and disgraced for opposing their messengers.

﴿Wa qad anzalna ayatin bayyinat﴾ (And We have certainly sent down clear signs): that is, while We have indeed sent down clear signs indicating the truthfulness of the Messenger.

﴿Adhabun muhin﴾ (a humiliating punishment): that is, it will bring them into disgrace and degradation.

﴿Yawma yab'athuhum Allahu jami'an﴾ (On the day when Allah will resurrect them all): that is, the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Ahsahu Allahu wa nasuhu﴾ (Allah has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it): that is, Allah has gathered and counted it, and they have forgotten it.

﴿Wa Allahu 'ala kulli shay'in shahid﴾ (And Allah is Witness over all things): that is, nothing among things is hidden from Him.

﴿Ma yakunu min najwa﴾ (There is no secret conversation): that is, among those conversing privately.

﴿Thalathatin illa huwa rabi'uhum﴾ (among three but He is their fourth): that is, He, exalted is He, is their fourth by His knowledge of them and His power over them.

﴿Wa la adna min dhalika﴾ (nor less than that): that is, fewer than three, which are two.

﴿Illa huwa ma'ahum ayna kanu﴾ (but He is with them wherever they are): that is, in any place on earth or in the heavens.

Explanation of the verses:

Allah's words ﴿Inna alladhina yuhadduna Allah wa rasulahu﴾: this verse carries good tidings to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), informing him of the defeat of the Quraysh, who gathered the confederates to fight him in the Battle of the Trench. Allah the Exalted said ﴿Inna alladhina yuhadduna Allah wa rasulahu﴾, that is, they oppose Allah and His Messenger and act as enemies to them both. ﴿Kubitu﴾ means they were humiliated and disgraced, ﴿kama kubita alladhina min qablihim﴾ as those before them were humiliated, those who denied their messengers, so Allah ﴿akbatahum﴾ abased them, that is, humbled and disgraced them.

As for Allah's words ﴿Wa qad anzalna ayatin bayyinat﴾: all of them indicate the truthfulness of Our Messenger in what he brought them and called them to, yet despite this they opposed him and fought him, therefore Allah abases and humiliates them in this world, and for the disbelievers there are their like, ﴿adhabun muhin﴾ a humiliating punishment on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿yawma yab'athuhum Allahu jami'an﴾ the Day when Allah resurrects them all, none of them left behind, and He will inform them of the evil and corruption they committed. ﴿Ahsahu Allah﴾: when His angels wrote it down, and it was written before their deed in the Book of Decrees, the Preserved Tablet, ﴿wa nasuhu﴾ and they forgot it because of the blindness of their hearts, their disbelief in their Lord and their meeting with Him, so they do not mention their sins until they repent of them and seek forgiveness. As for Allah's words ﴿Wa Allahu 'ala kulli shay'in shahid﴾: in addition to their deeds being recorded in the Preserved Tablet and the noble recording angels having written them, Allah the Exalted is Witness over all things, so nothing occurs except under His sight and knowledge.

As for Allah's words ﴿Alam tara anna Allaha ya'lamu ma fi as-samawati﴾: this is an affirmation of what preceded concerning the encompassing knowledge of Allah over all things, and that the deeds of those opposing, hostile transgressors are counted and known, and He will recompense them for them. That is, did you not know, O Our Messenger, that Allah the Exalted knows what is in the heavens and what is on earth, of subtle and grand things. It is reported that a group of hypocrites stayed behind, conversing privately among themselves to enrage the believers, so this verse was revealed alluding to them and uncovering their intentions. ﴿Ma yakunu min najwa﴾: that is, from those engaged in private conversation, ﴿thalatha illa huwa rabi'uhum﴾, that is, except that Allah the Exalted is their fourth by His knowledge of them and His power over them. This is the benefit of the companionship: knowledge and the power to seize and to give. ﴿Wa la khamsatin illa huwa sadisuhum﴾, and not five except He is their sixth, ﴿wa la adna min dhalika﴾ and not less than that, like two.

﴿Wa la akthara illa huwa ma'ahum﴾ and not more except that He is with them by His knowledge, power and encompassing, ﴿ayna kanu﴾ wherever they are, under the earth or above it in the heavens or below it. Then ﴿yunabbi'uhum﴾, that is, He informs and makes them know what they did on the Day of Resurrection, in order to recompense them for it. ﴿Inna Allaha bikulli shay'in 'alim﴾ is an affirmation of what preceded concerning His knowledge of those who oppose Him and of the hypocrites who are hostile to the believers, and He will recompense all of them with His justice, for He is the Mighty, the Wise.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Allah's severe warning of humiliation, disgrace and abasement for everyone who opposes Allah and His Messenger.

2- The encompassing knowledge of Allah over all things and His witnessing of all things and His enumeration of all the deeds of the servants, a state which necessitates watchfulness of Allah the Exalted, fear of Him, and the utmost shame before Him.

3- Guidance that private consultation for good should be among three, five or seven, so that one person serves as a just arbiter to tip the balance in disagreement; for when two disagree, there must be a third who tips the side of the disagreement, and when four disagree, there must be a fifth who tips the side of the disagreement.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 58, verse 8–10:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret consultation?﴾ That is, private speech in confidence; those forbidden were the Jews and the hypocrites.

﴿Then they return to what they were forbidden﴾: that is, to secret conferring deliberately, to harm the believers in Medina.

﴿And they confer together in sin and transgression﴾: that is, in what is sinful in itself, and in enmity toward the Messenger and the believers.

﴿And disobedience to the Messenger﴾: that is, they confer and some of them advise others to disobey the Messenger and not to obey him.

﴿And when they come to you, they greet you﴾: that is, when they come to you, O Prophet, they greet you with their words, "al-sam 'alayka" (death be upon you).

﴿with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾: that is, they greet you with the word "al-sam 'alayka," and Allah did not greet His Messenger with this; rather He greeted him with "al-salam 'alayka ayyuha al-nabi wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh" (peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings).

﴿And they say within themselves﴾: that is, secretly among themselves.

﴿Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?﴾: that is, why does Allah not punish us for what we say to him? For if he were a prophet, Allah would have hastened punishment upon us.

﴿Hell will be sufficient for them; they will burn in it, and wretched is the destination﴾: that is, the torment of Hell is sufficient for them, where they will burn, and wretched is their destination.

﴿So do not confer together in sin and transgression﴾: that is, let none of you confer with another in what is sinful, nor in what is transgression and wrongdoing, nor in what is disobedience to the Messenger.

﴿But confer together in righteousness and piety﴾: that is, and confer, if you wish to do so, in righteousness, meaning goodness, and piety, which is obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

﴿Secret conferring is only from Satan﴾: that is, secret conferring in sin and transgression is only from Satan, meaning by his deception.

﴿to grieve those who believe﴾: that is, to make them imagine that it is because of something that has happened which harms them.

﴿but it will not harm them at all, except by permission of Allah﴾: indeed, conferring does not harm the believers at all except by the will of Allah, the Exalted.

﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾: that is, upon Allah alone, not upon anyone else, should the believers rely.

The meaning of the verses:

Allah's words, ﴿Have you not seen…﴾ this verse was revealed concerning the Jews of Medina and the hypocrites among them. They used to confer in secret in the sight of the believers, and it was a time of war, so they would make the believers imagine that an enemy had resolved to attack them, or that a detachment had been defeated, or that a plot was being hatched against them. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade them from secret conferring and said, "No two should confer in private excluding a third." But they refused except to confer, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, expressing His wonder at them and threatening them after exposing them and uncovering the veil over their scheming against the believers and their deception toward them. So Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conferring, which is private conversation in front of people? Then they return to what they were forbidden, in disobedience and defiance toward the Messenger ﷺ, and they confer not in righteousness and piety but in sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger, that is, in what is sinful in itself, such as backbiting and foul speech, and in transgression, which is aggression against the believers and wronging them, and in disobedience to the Messenger, as some advise others to disobey the Messenger and not to obey his commands and prohibitions. And worse than this, when they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ they greeted him with a greeting by which Allah did not greet him; they did not say "al-salamu 'alaykum" but said "al-sam 'alaykum," and al-sam is death, twisting their tongues with it. They came to the Messenger one by one to greet him with this wicked greeting, wishing him death. May the curse of Allah be upon them; how much their harm, how severe their deceit, and how foul their wickedness. And they say within themselves, that is, among themselves: if Muhammad were a prophet, Allah would have seized us for what we say to him of invoking death upon him. This is the meaning of His words concerning them: ﴿And they say within themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ That is, why does Allah not punish us for what we say to Muhammad ﷺ if he were a prophet.

Allah said: ﴿Hell will be sufficient for them as punishment; they will burn in its heat and its blaze on the Day of Resurrection, and wretched is the destination to which they return in the Hereafter: Hell, with its zaqqum, its boiling water, its dari', its ghislin, and its yahmum. And beyond that, the wrath and curse of Allah are upon them.

And His words, ﴿O you who have believed, when you confer privately…﴾ This verse and the one after it were revealed for the spiritual upbringing and moral refinement of the believers. So Allah the Exalted said: O you who have believed, that is, who affirm Allah and His Messenger, when you confer privately for a matter that requires it of you, do not confer in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger, lest your state become like the state of the Jews and the hypocrites. But ﴿confer in righteousness and piety﴾, that is, in what is good in itself, free of sin, and in obedience to Allah and His Messenger, since these two are piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection for your reckoning and recompense, so fear Him by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger.

And His words: ﴿Secret conferring is only from Satan﴾, that is, he is the one who impels it and drives toward it, for the purpose of causing the believers grief and sorrow. Yet neither the conferring nor Satan can harm the believers at all except by the will of Allah, for lofty wisdoms known to Allah. Therefore do not grieve or be distressed by what you see of the conferring of your enemies, the Jews and the hypocrites, and rely upon Allah in all your affairs. And upon Allah the Exalted, not upon anyone else, let the believers rely in every time and place. For Allah the Exalted is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him; He suffices him in all that concerns him, and Allah is capable of that.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Clarification of the deceit and scheming of the Jews and the hypocrites against the believers in every time and place.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 58, verses 11–13:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Tafassahu fi al-majalis* (make room in the assemblies): i.e., widen the assemblies which are gatherings of knowledge and remembrance.

*Fa-ifsahu yafsahi Allahu lakum* (make room, and Allah will make room for you): i.e., in Paradise, in provision, and in the grave.

*Unshuzu fa-unshuzu* (rise up, so rise up): i.e., stand up for prayer or for other acts of righteousness.

*Yarfa'i Allahu alladhina amanu minkum* (Allah will raise those of you who believe): i.e., with victory and good remembrance in this world, and with lofty chambers in the Gardens in the Hereafter.

*Wa alladhina utu al-'ilma darajat* (and those who have been given knowledge, [will be raised] in ranks): i.e., and Allah will raise those who have been given knowledge to high ranks, for they combine knowledge and action.

*Idha naja'tumu al-Rasul* (when you consult the Messenger privately): i.e., when you wish to confer with him.

*Fa-qaddimu bayna yadayya najwakum sadaqatan* (then offer a charity before your private consultation): i.e., before the consultation, give a charity, then consult the Messenger (ﷺ).

*Dhalika khayrun lakum wa atharu* (that is better for you and purer): i.e., offering charity before private consultation is better for you because it benefits the poor, and purer for your sins.

*Fa-in lam tajidu* (but if you do not find [the means]): i.e., if you do not find anything to give in charity.

*Fa-inna Allaha ghafurun rahim* (then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful): i.e., He forgives your consultation and is merciful to you, so there is no sin upon you for consulting without a charity.

*A-ashfaqtum an tuqaddimu bayna yadayya najwakum sadaqat?* (Are you apprehensive about offering charities before your private consultations?): i.e., did you fear poverty if you offered charities before your private consultations?

*Fa-idh lam taf'alu wa tāba Allahu 'alaykum* (so when you do not do it, and Allah has forgiven you): i.e., offering the charities was lifted, and Allah turned to you by permitting you to abandon them.

*Fa-aqimu al-salat wa atu al-zakat* (so establish the prayer and give the zakat): i.e., perform the prayer in its required manner and pay the zakat.

*Wa atī'u Allaha wa Rasulahu* (and obey Allah and His Messenger): i.e., and persist in establishing the prayer, giving zakat, and obeying Allah and His Messenger.

*Wa Allahu khabirun bima ta'malun* (and Allah is Aware of what you do): i.e., of the acts of righteousness and good, and He will reward you for them with Paradise.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues with the training and refinement of the believers so that they may perfect themselves and be happy. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, i.e., who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, ﴿when you are told, "Make room in the assemblies"﴾, i.e., when the Messenger (ﷺ) or someone else says to you, make room in the gathering so that others may find a place among you. So make room and do not be stingy about being close to the Messenger, or to the scholar who teaches you, or to the reminder who admonishes you. And if you make room, i.e., Allah, the Exalted, will reward you: He will widen [your provision] for you in this world with abundance of sustenance, in the barzakh in the grave, and in the Hereafter in the lofty chambers of Paradise.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when it is said, "Rise up"﴾, i.e., rise from the assembly for a reason, or for prayer, or for fighting, or for an act of righteousness and good. ﴿So rise up﴾, i.e., move quickly and stand up, and Allah will reward you. ﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe﴾ in ranks, with victory and good remembrance in this world, and in the chambers of Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿And those who have been given knowledge [will be raised] in ranks﴾, i.e., and Allah will raise those among you, O believers, who have been given knowledge to high ranks, for they combine faith, knowledge and action.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ reminds them, the Exalted, of His knowledge of them in all their states, so that they may be mindful of Him, increase in obedience to Him, and guard their piety.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, offer a charity before your private consultation﴾: He, the Exalted, commanded them, when one of them wished to consult the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and speak with him alone, to first give a charity and then request the consultation. This was first for the benefit of the poor, and then to lighten the burden on the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), since every believer wishes to be alone with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to draw near to him and speak with him, and the Messenger is a human being who cannot accommodate everyone. So Allah legislated this charity, informing them that He wished to lighten the burden on His Messenger.

When they knew this, and found it difficult to give charity, and most of them were poor and could not find it, Allah abrogated it, and the period of obligation did not last more than a few nights. He abrogated it by His saying that follows: ﴿Are you apprehensive...﴾, the verse.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is better for you and purer﴾, i.e., offering charity before private consultation is better for you, since the charity returns to the poor, your brothers, and purer, i.e., for your souls, because the soul is purified by righteous action. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But if you do not find [the means]﴾, i.e., the charity to offer before the consultation, then consult him (ﷺ), and there is no blame upon you for not finding it. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving to you and Merciful to you.﴾

His saying: ﴿Are you apprehensive...?﴾, i.e., did you fear poverty and want if you were obliged to give charity before every private consultation? Accordingly, if you do not do it, and Allah turns to you by lifting this obligation and abrogating it, returning you to the state before the obligation of charity, then establish the prayer by performing it at its times, in the congregation of the believers, observing its conditions, pillars, sunnahs and etiquette, and give the obligatory zakat on your wealth. Obey Allah and His Messenger in their commands and prohibitions; that will suffice you in place of the charity that was abrogated, as a lightening and a mercy to you.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, i.e., so be mindful of Him in obedience to Him and to His Messenger, that you may prosper, be saved from the Fire, and enter Paradise, the abode of the righteous.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Encouragement to the virtue of making room in gatherings of knowledge and remembrance.

2- Encouragement and exhortation to doing good and fulfilling obligations when a believer is called to them.

3- The virtue of faith and the excellence of knowledge and acting upon it.

4- The legitimacy of abrogation (naskh) in the Sharia, both before and after acting upon the abrogated ruling, since this charity was abrogated before anyone acted upon it, except for what was done by ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), who reported that he gave a dinar in charity and consulted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then this charity was abrogated. He used to say: "There is a verse in the Qur'an that no one acted upon but me," and this is a virtue for him (may Allah be pleased with him).

5- In establishing prayer, giving zakat, and obeying Allah and His Messenger in obligations and prohibitions is a substitute for what the believer misses of voluntary acts.

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of allying with the Jews.

2- The prohibition of swearing upon falsehood, which is the perjurous oath (al-yamin al-ghamus).

3- Among the signs of Shaytan's domination over a person is his leaving the remembrance of Allah with his heart and tongue, and his neglect of His promise and threat through his deeds and words.

﴿Wa ayyadahum bi-ruhin minhu﴾: that is, with proof, light and guidance.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs the believers, guiding them to the straightest path and the most perfect condition, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, who oppose them in their command and prohibition and in what they call to of the true religion, ﴿those are among the most humiliated﴾, that is, the opponents are among the group of the abased in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And He supported them with a spirit from Himself﴾, that is, with proof and light from Him, glory be to Him and exalted is He. This is in this world. As for the Hereafter, He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, that is, lush orchards through which various rivers flow among the trees and palaces, abiding therein forever, never to leave them. And above all that, Allah is pleased with them for their obedience to Him, and they are pleased with Him in the Hereafter by His admitting them into Paradise, the abode of the God-fearing.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the party of Allah﴾, that is, those who are elevated in their spiritual perfections are the party of Allah, meaning His army and allies. Then He announced their success and triumph, saying: ﴿Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful﴾, that is, the ones who will triumph on the Day of Resurrection by deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Allah has decreed humiliation and disgrace upon whoever opposes Him and His Messenger by defying them in what they love and dislike.

2- Allah, exalted is He, decreed the victory of His Messenger, and He gives victory; indeed He is Strong, Mighty.

3- Befriending a disbeliever with support and love is forbidden, even if he is the closest of relatives. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah fought their fathers, sons, brothers and tribes at Badr, and this verse was revealed concerning them, giving them good news of Allah's pleasure with them and His favor upon them. O Allah, make us among them and gather us in their company.
